\chapter{Communication Complexity — Det Rectangle}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.DetRectangle
\section{Overview}

This module establishes that every deterministic communication protocol induces a
monochromatic rectangle partition of the input space $X \times Y$ into at most
$2^c$ rectangles, where $c$ is the protocol's communication complexity.
It also derives the fooling-set lower-bound method, showing that the size of any
fooling set bounds $\mathrm{CC}(g)$ from below via $\lceil \log_2 |S| \rceil \leq \mathrm{CC}(g)$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Swap of a protocol input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\leanok
Given a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, $\texttt{swapInputSet}(R)$ is the set
$\{(y, x) \mid (x, y) \in R\} \subseteq Y \times X$ obtained by swapping the two
coordinates of every element.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the coordinate-swapped set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_swapInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
Let $R \subseteq X \times Y$, and write $\mathrm{swap}(R) = \{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in R\}
\subseteq Y \times X$ for the set obtained by exchanging the two coordinates of every
element of $R$. Then for any pair $(y, x) \in Y \times X$, one has $(y, x) \in
\mathrm{swap}(R)$ if and only if $(x, y) \in R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate swap is an involution]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_swapInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, swapping the two coordinates of every element
twice returns the original set: writing $\mathrm{swap}(R) = \{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in R\}$,
one has $\mathrm{swap}(\mathrm{swap}(R)) = R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Preimage of a protocol input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\leanok
Given maps $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ and a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$,
$\texttt{preimageInputSet}(f_X, f_Y, R)$ is the set
$\{(x', y') \in X' \times Y' \mid (f_X(x'), f_Y(y')) \in R\}$, the pullback of $R$ along
the product map $f_X \times f_Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the pullback of a protocol input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_preimageInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_preimageInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be maps, let $R \subseteq X \times Y$, and let
$(x', y') \in X' \times Y'$. Then $(x', y')$ lies in the pullback of $R$ along the
product map $f_X \times f_Y$ if and only if $(f_X(x'), f_Y(y')) \in R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Auxiliary leaf rectangles relative to a constraint]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p006-b005,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p007-b002,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p007-b004
}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b002}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol}
For a protocol $p$ and sets $A \subseteq X$, $B \subseteq Y$, $\texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, A, B)$
is the collection of rectangles induced by the leaves of $p$ when the reachable inputs are
constrained to $A \times B$. It is defined by structural recursion: an output node yields
$\{A \times B\}$, while Alice (resp.\ Bob) nodes split $A$ (resp.\ $B$) according to the
branching function and recurse.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p006-b005,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p004-b005
}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b002}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
The \emph{leaf rectangles} of a protocol $p : \texttt{Protocol}\,X\,Y\,\alpha$ form the
collection $\texttt{leafRectangles}(p) = \texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, X, Y)$, i.e.\ the set
of input rectangles induced by the leaves of $p$ over the full input space $X \times Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate swap commutes with role swap on leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_cover, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$
(Bob), and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Denote by $p^{\mathrm{sw}}$ the
role-swapped protocol over $Y \times X$ obtained by exchanging Alice and Bob throughout,
and for a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$ write $R^{\mathrm{sw}} = \{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in
R\} \subseteq Y \times X$ for its coordinate swap. Then for every rectangle $R$ in the
collection of auxiliary leaf rectangles of $p$ relative to $A \times B$, the swapped set
$R^{\mathrm{sw}}$ belongs to the collection of auxiliary leaf rectangles of
$p^{\mathrm{sw}}$ relative to $B \times A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Role swap sends leaf rectangles to their coordinate swaps]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_swap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob), and let $p^{\mathrm{swap}}$ be the protocol over $Y \times X$ obtained by
exchanging the roles of Alice and Bob throughout. If $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is one of
the leaf rectangles of $p$, then its coordinate swap $\{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in R\}
\subseteq Y \times X$ is one of the leaf rectangles of $p^{\mathrm{swap}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pullback preserves leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_comap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_comap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.comap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$, let $A
\subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be
arbitrary maps. If $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is one of the leaf rectangles of $p$
relative to the constraint $A \times B$, then its pullback along $f_X \times f_Y$,
namely $\{(x', y') \in X' \times Y' \mid (f_X(x'), f_Y(y')) \in R\}$, is one of the leaf
rectangles of the pulled-back protocol $\mathrm{comap}(p, f_X, f_Y)$ relative to the
constraint $f_X^{-1}(A) \times f_Y^{-1}(B)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leaf rectangles are preserved under input pull-back]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_comap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_comap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.comap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_comap}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$ producing
values in $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be arbitrary maps.
Write $p'$ for the protocol over $X' \times Y'$ obtained from $p$ by pre-composing every
message function with $f_X$ or $f_Y$ as appropriate. If $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is a
leaf rectangle of $p$, then its pullback $\{(x', y') \in X' \times Y' \mid (f_X(x'),
f_Y(y')) \in R\}$ along the product map $f_X \times f_Y$ is a leaf rectangle of $p'$.
\end{theorem}

and $Y$ (Bob), and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Then every set belonging to
the auxiliary leaf-rectangle collection of $p$ relative to the constraint $A \times B$
is a rectangle; that is, if $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is one of these leaf sets, then $R
= A' \times B'$ for some $A' \subseteq X$ and $B' \subseteq Y$.

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_isRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice's inputs drawn
from $X$ and Bob's from $Y$, and let $R$ belong to the collection of leaf rectangles of
$p$ over the full input space $X \times Y$. Then $R$ is a rectangle: there exist subsets
$A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$ with $R = A \times B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Auxiliary leaf rectangles lie within the constraint]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_subset}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_subset}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob), and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Then every rectangle $R$ in
the collection of auxiliary leaf rectangles of $p$ constrained to $A \times B$ satisfies
$R \subseteq A \times B$.
\end{lemma}

from a set $X$, Bob's inputs from a set $Y$, and outputs in a type $\alpha$, and let $A
\subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Then the rectangle $A \times B$ is contained in the
union of the auxiliary leaf rectangles of $p$ relative to the constraint $A \times B$;
that is, every pair $(x, y) \in A \times B$ lies in at least one rectangle of this
collection.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$
(Bob) producing values of type $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. If
$R$ and $S$ are two distinct rectangles in the collection of auxiliary leaf rectangles
of $p$ relative to $A$ and $B$, then $R$ and $S$ are disjoint as subsets of $X \times
Y$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$
producing values in $\alpha$, and let $R$ and $S$ be two of its leaf rectangles, that
is, two of the input rectangles induced by the leaves of $p$ over $X \times Y$. If $R
\neq S$, then $R$ and $S$ are disjoint as subsets of $X \times Y$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$
(Bob) with outputs in $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. If $R$ is
one of the auxiliary leaf rectangles of $p$ constrained to $A \times B$, and $(x, y)$
and $(x', y')$ both belong to $R$, then running $p$ yields the same output at both
inputs; that is, $p(x, y) = p(x', y')$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$
with output type $\alpha$, and let $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function that $p$
computes, meaning that running $p$ on any pair of inputs $(x, y)$ returns $g\,x\,y$.
Then every leaf rectangle $R$ of $p$ is monochromatic for $g$: the value $g\,x\,y$ is
the same for all $(x, y) \in R$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob), and let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Then the number of distinct
rectangles among the auxiliary leaf rectangles of $p$ relative to the constraint $A
\times B$ is at most $2^{c}$, where $c$ is the communication complexity of $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Finiteness of the auxiliary leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_finite}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_finite}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication
protocol over inputs $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with outputs in $\alpha$, and let $A
\subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$. Then the collection of leaf rectangles induced by $p$
when its reachable inputs are constrained to $A \times B$ is finite.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Finiteness of a protocol's leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_finite}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_finite}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_finite, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles}
\difficulty{1}
For any deterministic two-party communication protocol $p$ over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) producing values in $\alpha$, the collection of leaf rectangles of $p$ —
the input rectangles in $X \times Y$ induced by the leaves of $p$ over the full input
space — is finite.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.Computes, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_cover, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_disjoint, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_mono, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$
producing outputs in $\alpha$, and let $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$. If $p$ computes $g$,
then the collection of leaf rectangles of $p$ is a monochromatic rectangle partition of
$X \times Y$ for $g$: every leaf rectangle is a rectangle and is monochromatic for $g$,
the leaf rectangles cover all of $X \times Y$, and any two distinct leaf rectangles are
disjoint.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol on input types $X$ and $Y$
with output type $\alpha$, and let $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function that $p$
computes. Then the leaf rectangles of $p$ form a monochromatic rectangle partition of $X
\times Y$ for $g$; that is, they are pairwise disjoint rectangles covering $X \times Y$,
each of which is monochromatic for $g$. Moreover, the number of leaf rectangles is at
most $2^{c}$, where $c$ is the communication complexity of $p$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.SubprotocolPath, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.reachXPath, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.reachYPath, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.reachesPath, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\difficulty{2}
Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over Alice's input
type $X$ and Bob's input type $Y$, and let $\pi$ be a subprotocol path witnessing that
$s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$. Then the set of input pairs
\[
\{(x, y) \in X \times Y : (x,y) \text{ reaches } s \text{ along } \pi\}
\]
is a rectangle. Explicitly, it factors as $A \times B$, where $A \subseteq X$ is the set
of Alice inputs consistent with every one of Alice's branching choices along $\pi$ and
$B \subseteq Y$ is the set of Bob inputs consistent with every one of Bob's branching
choices along $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication
protocol over Alice's inputs $X$ and Bob's inputs $Y$ with outputs in $\alpha$, and
suppose $s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$. Then the set of input pairs $(x, y) \in X \times
Y$ that reach $s$ — those for which $x$ lies in Alice's reach set and $y$ lies in Bob's
reach set — is a rectangle: it factors as a product $A \times B$ for some $A \subseteq
X$ and $B \subseteq Y$.
\end{theorem}

  {CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition}
  {direct}
  {raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}
  {pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b003,
    pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b005}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_card, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{2}
Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function, and let $n$ be a natural
number. If the deterministic communication complexity $D(g)$ satisfies $D(g) \le n$,
then there is a collection $\mathcal{P}$ of subsets of $X \times Y$ that is a
monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$ — every member is a rectangle, every member is
monochromatic for $g$, the members cover $X \times Y$, and distinct members are disjoint
— and whose number of parts satisfies $\abs{\mathcal{P}} \le 2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rectangle-partition lower bound on communication complexity]

\difficulty{4}
Let $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function and let $n$ be a natural number.
If every monochromatic rectangle partition of $g$ consists of strictly more than $2^n$
parts, then the deterministic communication complexity of $g$ satisfies $n + 1 \le
D(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_card, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_finite, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.foolingSet_ncard_le_of_monoPartition}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function, and let $S \subseteq X
\times Y$ be a fooling set for $g$, meaning that $S$ meets every $g$-monochromatic
rectangle in at most one point. If the deterministic communication complexity of $g$
satisfies $D(g) \le n$ for some $n \in \bbn$, then the cardinality of $S$ satisfies
$\abs{S} \le 2^{n}$.
\end{theorem}

  {CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.foolingSet_ncard_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.foolingSet_ncard_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function and let $S \subseteq X \times
Y$ be a fooling set for $g$, meaning that every rectangle that is monochromatic for $g$
meets $S$ in at most one point. Then the deterministic communication complexity of $g$
satisfies
\[
  \lceil \log_2 \abs{S} \rceil \;\le\; D(g),
\]
where $\abs{S}$ is the number of elements of $S$ and both sides are compared in
$\bbn_\infty$.
\end{theorem}
